issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template Stock class provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This name/signature mismatch is structural: students will be guided by the specification (emptyStock) and the UML, but the starter code uses a different method name, which can confuse them or cause compilation/test failures when they try to follow the spec.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (preferred, to match the UML and solution), or update the problem statement and solution to reference clearInventory(). Ensure the method signature is public void emptyStock() in the template Stock class so students implement/use the expected API.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML expect a Stock.emptyStock() method, but the template Stock class defines a method named clearInventory(). The solution implements emptyStock(). This naming mismatch (emptyStock vs. clearInventory) creates a mapping confusion: students reading the problem will look for or be asked to implement emptyStock(), but the provided template uses a different identifier, which may lead to failed tests or wasted time locating/renaming the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() to match the problem statement and UML. Alternatively, add an emptyStock() wrapper in the template that calls clearInventory() so both names are supported.
